name: Decca
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Decca, also called Deoca, was an Irish princess of Munster in the seventh century. She married the king of Connacht. In the saga of the Children of Lir, one of the Three Sorrows of Ireland, she heard a tale of singing swans. These were the enchanted Fionnuala and her four brothers, whose human voices stayed in their transformed bodies. Decca demanded to see them. Her husband refused, so she left him. He then gave in and brought the swans to their palace. Decca watched as the swans regained their human shape at that very moment, only to die of advanced age and turn to dust before her eyes.

okr.objective: Records Decca, the Munster princess who saw the swans of the Children of Lir at their last change.
